summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests tislelizumab, a PD-1 blocking drug, in people with mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colorectal cancer who live in Nigeria. Tislelizumab is given as an IV infusion of 200 mg every 3 weeks, with the first infusion over 60 minutes and later ones over 30 minutes, until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, death, or completion of 104 weeks (35 doses). The record does not state a primary outcome measure, but says the study will look at whether the drug is effective and at its safety.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa tislelizumab, un fármaco que bloquea PD-1, en personas con cáncer colorrectal con deficiencia en la reparación de errores de apareamiento (dMMR) que viven en Nigeria. El tislelizumab se administra por vía intravenosa a 200 mg cada 3 semanas; la primera infusión dura 60 minutos y las siguientes 30 minutos, hasta progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad inaceptable, retiro del estudio, muerte o completar 104 semanas (35 dosis). El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal, pero señala que el estudio analizará si el fármaco es eficaz y su seguridad.
who_for: No prior treatment for the cancer, with dMMR colorectal cancer confirmed by immunohistochemistry
Metastatic disease not eligible for curative surgery, or stage II or III rectal cancer without distant spread
Adequate blood, kidney, liver and clotting test results within 14 days of start
not_for: Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, or prior grade 3 or higher immune-related side effects
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic therapy within the past 2 years
History of interstitial lung disease, noninfectious pneumonitis, or uncontrolled lung disease
Recent heart or blood vessel events (such as heart attack or stroke within 6 months), or pregnancy or breastfeeding
